newsitem.title: LATVIA: LPA URGES BLUE CHIPS TO REVIEW '97 FORECASTS.
newsitem.headline: LPA URGES BLUE CHIPS TO REVIEW '97 FORECASTS.

text.p: The privatisation agency (LPA) on Wednesday said leading Riga stock exchange shares should increase efficiency and revise their 1997 profit forecasts upwards to maintain activity on the local capital markets.
Volumes on the Riga bourse have fallen steeply lately as investors have switched from securities to vouchers ahead of the privatisation of big utility companies later this year.
Lower profit forecasts for 1997 compared to 1996 by leading companies was a major factor behind the bourse's sluggish performance, LPA manager Janis Naglis told a news conference.
"To my mind the boards (of the five leading stocks) should make corrections in their forecasts and make decisions leading to increased efficiency," Naglis said.
Daugavpils Chain maker, which has applied for a transfer to the official list, earlier said it expects a 1997 profit of 615,000 lats against 1.06 million lats in 1996.
Kaija fish cannery also gave a lower 1997 forecast of 639,893 lats against 1.1 million lats last year.
Leading bank Unibanka has said it expects profit no less than the 5.97 million lats it made in 1996.
